newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Leader says make S.Lanka south Asia financial hub.
newsitem.headline: Leader says make S.Lanka south Asia financial hub.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga said her government plans to give more concessions to the financial sector in the forthcoming budget to help Sri Lanka become the financial hub of south Asia.

"Becoming a financial hub of this region is an attainable reality. But time is of essence. We have to seize the moment and start the process now," the state-run daily News on Saturday quoted Kumaratunga as saying.
"The private and public sectors will have to work more closely to achieve this objective. The government will extend its fullest cooperation to this effort," Kumaratunga said.
Next year's budget is due to be presented in parliament in November.
She said the financial sector should exploit the country's location, manpower resources and sufficient infrastructure to promote Sri Lanka as a major financial centre.

"We only have to inject a new level of commitment to the public service to get its fullest participation in the process. That is the responsibility of the government and we will see that is done," Kumaratunga was quoted a saying at the inauguration of a new Bank of Ceylon building.

Kumaratunga has been critical of the bureaucracy lately. She has said public service, which has been accused of being lethargic, inefficient and corrupt, was a far bigger problem for the country than the 14-year-old ethnic war in the northeast.
She said the policies of her People's Alliance government had boosted investor confidence after a fall in interest rates and inflation this year.
